RFC 020: RFC 019 Execution Review

Development Team Review and Applied Adjustments

Published

January 19, 2026

Executive Summary

RFC 019 was executed as a structured development team review to confirm that the multi-route serve model is clear, testable, and ready for implementation. The review focused on configuration completeness, validation guardrails, and operational determinism. The outcome is a set of applied clarifications in RFC 019 that tighten defaults, normalization rules, and routing behavior without expanding scope.

Review Method

The review followed the RFC 019 prompt and captured decisions as explicit adjustments to the document. Roles are listed to document coverage rather than to identify individuals.

Table 1. Development team review coverage.
Role Focus Output
Product lead Requirements clarity Gaps in operator intent and defaults.
Pipeline engineer Technical feasibility Normalization and routing edge cases.
QA/validation Testability Validation rules and failure modes.
Operations Runbook readiness Route enablement and overlap behavior.

Findings and Decisions

Table 2. Review findings and applied decisions.
Finding Impact Decision Action
recursive appears in the example but not in the field list. Documentation mismatch for routing behavior. Document the field and its defaulting rule. Added a validation row for recursive.
file_globs normalization from string to list is implied but not explicit. Inconsistent parsing and tests. Make normalization explicit. Clarified normalization in the table and narrative.
priority default is not specified. Ambiguous overlap handling. Define a default and keep error on ties. Documented default 0 and tie behavior.
Disabled routes are not explicitly excluded from overlap checks. Potential false validation errors. Exclude disabled routes from overlap validation. Added routing rule on disabled routes.
id derivation rule is implicit. Inconsistent IDs across configs. Define derived ID behavior. Clarified derivation in the field table.
NoteDecision

RFC 019 remains the authoritative multi-route plan, and this RFC records the review and the applied clarifications.

Applied Adjustments to RFC 019

Table 3. Adjustments incorporated into RFC 019.
Area Change Rationale
Configuration table Documented recursive and file_globs normalization. Aligns docs with example and parser expectations.
Configuration defaults Clarified priority default and id derivation. Prevents ambiguous routing and ID drift.
Routing rules Excluded disabled routes from overlap validation. Avoids false positives for staged rollouts.

Next Steps

The plan is ready for implementation sequencing. If desired, we can now open tickets corresponding to Sprint 1 tasks and align test scaffolding with the clarified rules.

Appendix A: Review Prompt Used

Please review RFC 019 for clarity, completeness, and any missing technical details. Identify gaps in validation coverage, propose improvements to the routing rules, and suggest additional sprint tasks that improve traceability or operational safety.
